_comment: Baseline for ci/check_orphan_cores.py (the wire-or-delete ratchet, DD review §8.2). Every entry is a crate-root `pub mod` with no detected non-test consumer, allowed to stay with the justification given. Adding an entry requires a justification reviewed in the PR that adds it; removing entries (because the module gained a consumer or was deleted) never needs review. Detection is textual — trait-impl seams and feature-gated FFI consumers are its known blind spots, and such entries say so.

allowed_orphans.kirra_fleet_transport::transport: Zenoh carrier module. Only appearances outside its own tree are the `pub mod` line and re-exports, which this gate discounts. Pre-existing condition the bare-identifier scan hid; wiring or deleting it is its owner's call.
allowed_orphans.kirra_map::lanelet2: Feature-gated Lanelet2 cxx FFI bridge (`lanelet2` feature, off by default); its consumer is the ros2+lanelet2 node build, outside the default-feature textual scan.
allowed_orphans.kirra_ota_installer::nvbootctrl: Jetson bootloader A/B controller: Installer-driven and unit-tested over a mock, with no non-test caller until the rootfs-level A/B driver lands (docs/ota/ROOTFS_AB_DESIGN.md). Pre-existing; exposed 2026-08-08.
allowed_orphans.kirra_persistence::schema_spec: Cross-backend schema conformance spec (#1033/P-Schema): its consumers are the SQLite and Postgres conformance TEST suites by design -- a runtime caller would be wrong, like the traceability_gate and wcet_gate entries. Exposed 2026-08-08 when `src/tests.rs`-style test modules stopped counting as production consumers.
allowed_orphans.kirra_planner::lanelet2: Same feature-gated Lanelet2 bridge, planner side — consumed only under the `lanelet2` feature build.
allowed_orphans.kirra_trajectory::redundancy_hardening: Verification-hardening module by design: its consumers are the property/hardening test suites; it backs the True-Redundancy cross_check evidence, not a runtime path.
allowed_orphans.kirra_verifier::dds_cyclonedds: CycloneDDS binding, reached only through a feature-gated build path outside the default-feature textual scan. Pre-existing; exposed 2026-08-08.
allowed_orphans.kirra_verifier::spi_ledger: Safety-performance-indicator ledger. No consumer anywhere: SpiRegistry appears in no non-test source outside its own module. Exposed 2026-08-08 by the collision fix (`evaluate`/`passed` are ubiquitous names it was being credited for). A real unwired core, recorded rather than silently carried; wiring or deleting it is its owner's call, not this gate fix's.
allowed_orphans.kirra_verifier::traceability_gate: CI gate by design: runs as a test lane (SAFETY:/REQ:/TEST: tag coverage); a runtime consumer would be wrong.
allowed_orphans.kirra_verifier::wcet_gate: CI gate by design: the O(1) structural-boundedness WCET guard runs as a test lane; a runtime consumer would be wrong.
allowed_orphans.kirra_world::kind: ObservationKind/TypedBody, ruled by KIRRA-WM-OBSKIND-001 (2026-08-07). Re-exported from the crate root and referenced in prose, but NOT YET INVOKED: nothing constructs a TypedBody or branches on a kind. Exposed 2026-08-08 when the gate stopped crediting colliding item names (`as_str`/`from_token`) as consumption -- a PRE-EXISTING condition the gate was blind to, not new debt. Heals when the store's payload path types its body instead of carrying opaque TEXT.
allowed_orphans.kirra_world::same_as_adjudication: Tier 2 box 2b, deliberately unwired: 2c (deterministic resolution over promoted identity) is its first consumer, exactly as 2a was unwired until 2b. It is the SECOND half of the propose -> adjudicate boundary; wiring it to a producer before 2c exists would mean inventing the consumer to satisfy a gate. Heals when 2c consumes confirmed_relations/corroboration_count; ci/test_orphan_cores.py asserts 2a is now consumed BY this module, which is the wiring event that retired its own baseline entry.
allowed_orphans.kirra_world_store::retention_driver: Retention driver: test-covered, no runtime caller until the retention scheduler is wired. Pre-existing; exposed 2026-08-08.
allowed_orphans.kirra_world_store::retention_sweeper: Retention sweeper, same state as its sibling retention_driver. Pre-existing; exposed 2026-08-08.
allowed_orphans.parko_core::control_loop: Parko inference/control loop. Reachable only through a crate-root `pub use`, which this gate deliberately discounts -- a shelf with a label is still a shelf. Exposed 2026-08-08 by the collision fix (`state`/`tick`/`with_clock`/`with_governor` are names several modules export). Heals when parko-ros2's node drives it rather than re-exporting it.
allowed_orphans.parko_core::detector: Detection decode path (BBox/Detection/decode_detections) awaiting the real-perception integration (external track, MGA G-4); test-covered, no runtime consumer until sensors land.
allowed_orphans.parko_ros2::image_shim: ROS 2 message-conversion shim awaiting the sensor integration (external track, MGA G-4); consumed by the ros2-feature node build once camera input lands.
allowed_orphans.parko_ros2::odometry_shim: ROS 2 message-conversion shim awaiting the sensor integration (external track, MGA G-4).
allowed_orphans.parko_ros2::radar_shim: ROS 2 message-conversion shim awaiting the sensor integration (external track, MGA G-4).
allowed_orphans.parko_ros2::pointcloud2_shim: ROS 2 message-conversion shim awaiting the sensor integration (external track, MGA G-4) — the fourth of four, alongside image_shim/odometry_shim/radar_shim. Added 2026-08-19 by the consumer-attribution audit (docs/design/ORPHAN_GATE_FALLOUT.md), which found it in the SAME unwired state as its three siblings while the gate credited it: it exports a constant `INT8`, and parko-core writes `PrecisionMode::INT8` — an unrelated enum variant, in a crate that does not depend on parko-ros2 at all. `ambiguous_item_names` could not see the collision because that guard discounts names owned by two scanned MODULES and this one is with an enum variant. Not new debt; debt that was invisible. Heals when the ros2-feature node build consumes it, like its siblings. EXPECTED WARNING: until rules A and B land, this gate reports this entry [HEALED] and advises removing it — because the very credit this entry documents as false is the credit the gate still counts. Do NOT remove it on that advice; the entry is what makes the stronger detector land with zero new red instead of a wall nobody has classified.
allowed_orphans.parko_core::backend_selector: Backend-selection registry (BackendSelector/register_backend_factory/TargetPlatform) awaiting a backend crate that registers itself; none does today, and the ONNX/OpenVINO/TensorRT crates are hardware/CI-gated. Same family as parko_core::detector. Added 2026-08-19 by the consumer-attribution audit (docs/design/ORPHAN_GATE_FALLOUT.md): the gate credited it on two lines inside its OWN crate's `pub use backend_selector::{ … };`, because REEXPORT_RE is line-anchored and rustfmt wrapped the item names onto the following lines — the 'shelf with a label' the gate excludes, admitted through its own front door. Verified zero non-comment references to any of its eight exported items repo-wide. Heals when a backend registers. EXPECTED WARNING: until rules A and B land, this gate reports this entry [HEALED] and advises removing it — because the very credit this entry documents as false is the credit the gate still counts. Do NOT remove it on that advice; the entry is what makes the stronger detector land with zero new red instead of a wall nobody has classified.
